newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian CPI up 0.31 pct in September.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian CPI up 0.31 pct in September.

text.p: The Palestinian consumer price index (CPI) in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Arab East Jerusalem rose 0.31 percent in September, a Palestinian official said on Tuesday.
This follows a 0.7 percent increase in August.

Hazem al-Shunnar, in charge of economic statistics at the Palestinian Statistics Department, said the rise brought inflation to 8.2 percent between November 1995 -- when the department began calculating the index -- and September 1996.
"The rise was in all main sectors," Shunnar said, adding that the sharpest increases were in health care and education.
He said the highest rise was in Gaza, where the CPI jumped by 1.1 percent, compared to a rise of 0.34 percent in East Jerusalem and 0.18 percent in the West Bank.
Shunnar attributed the high rise in Gaza to an Israeli closure imposed late in September on the Palestinian areas following gunbattles between PLO police and Israeli troops.
He said unlike the West Bank, which continued to import some goods from Israel despite the closure, Gaza was completely cut off, causing prices to go up.
